external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who use their own identity provider to sign in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the franchise identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: own devices
external_entities.description: Colleagues' own devices used to sign in from home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies group membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for them to the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, validates federated sign-ins, and supplies public signing-key material to applications.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker runs on the corporate network. Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in. Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires. Nor has anyone written down whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their groups.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership is supplied by the HR system overnight. Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what that log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Nobody has written down whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues use their own devices at home to sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing the colleague's staff id and groups

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the identity broker using their own identity provider's vouching.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: provide token
data_flows.description: The identity broker provides a token to the store admin console for authorization.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: manage store
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions
data_flows.data_description: Store-manager token and price or transaction operations

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: store signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull membership
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls colleague and group membership changes from the HR system once a night.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker updates its directory with colleagues and group membership.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-in
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down whether this covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home
trust_boundaries.description: The home location of colleagues' own devices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment containing franchise colleagues and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it records colleague sign-ins.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the audit log records sign-ins.
